reasoning.summary:
Week 7 moneyline sweep. Each game got a team rating built from every completed 2025 and 2026 game: an opponent-adjusted margin rating (70%) plus a yardage-efficiency lens (30%), blended 50/50 across the two seasons. Confirmed QB news adjusted it by hand: Lamar out, Hurts out, McCarthy starting, Mayfield back. The final win chance was 40% model and 60% no-vig market. ESPN FPI was checked last, and it could move confidence by at most one step.

The ticket stacks nine favorites to reach about $216 on $5 with the 25% acca boost. Not one favorite was priced more than about 1.5% under the model, so the ticket was negative EV at the book's prices before it was placed. It was a payout ticket, not an edge ticket. Two of the nine legs (NYJ, DET) were added by the user on top of Sofa's tiers.

Not PF-grounded: PropFinder has no NFL game board.

legs.NYJ ML: The model had NYJ 56%, against 69% implied at -220. The final blend was 61.9%. FPI agreed (65%). MIA was 0-5, but MIA swept NYJ in 2025. Added by the user; the model rated it below the price.
legs.DET ML: Model 54.5%, final 58.8%, FPI 59%. GB won both 2025 meetings. Added by the user; the model was below the -196 price.
legs.HOU ML: The strongest lean on the slate. Model 68.5%, final 75.1%, FPI 85%. The NYG downgrade for McCarthy starting was already in. Placed at -500, below the model.
legs.MIN ML: Model 62.8%, final 69.1%, FPI 65%. Placed at -310. The market moved further toward MIN before kickoff (closed -340).
legs.LAR ML: One of the three legs where the model was at or above the market (62.4% vs 60.9%). FPI 67%. Garrett on IR cost LAR 0.5 points. The line closed at -192, so the -170 entry beat the close.
legs.SEA ML: Model 58.7% vs 57.2% market, so the model was at or above the market. FPI disagreed (KC 53%), and no missed fact explained the gap, so the data lean stood.
legs.PIT ML: Model 58.6% at the neutral site in Paris; the market and FPI agreed.
legs.SF ML: Model 56.5% vs 60% implied. Bosa was out, and SF won the 2025 meeting 20-10. FPI agreed strongly (79%).
legs.DEN ML: Model 54.9% vs 69% implied. DEN's yardage margin (-111 per game) was the weak spot. FPI agreed (69%). It made the ticket only for payout.

review.summary:
Lost: 6 of 9 legs hit (NYJ, HOU and SF lost).

With nine favorites at these prices, about six wins was the expected result. The sum of the implied probabilities was about 6.1, and all nine hitting was about a 3% chance with the vig in. So the outcome was normal.

The pattern is the useful part. All three losers were legs where the model was at or below the price. The legs where the model was at or above the market (LAR, PIT, SEA) went 3-0, and LAR also beat the closing line. This is the 10-23 NBA rule (no favorite ML unless the model's probability is at least the implied price) showing up in a second sport.

Change for next time: drop model-below-market favorites, even when they're the user's adds, or keep the ticket to three or four legs.

legs.NYJ ML: MIA won 28-25. The model was 13 points below the price, and the 2025 sweep had already flagged the matchup.
legs.HOU ML: NYG won 27-21 in OT. At -500 this was the most expensive leg, and the model had it 15 points under the price. The heavy juice bought very little safety.
legs.SF ML: ATL won 29-20. This was the only placed leg that drifted against us before kickoff (-151 to -142), so the market moved off SF.

reasoning.summary:
A shorter ticket built from the strongest pieces of the Best 6: the biggest model gap (BKN +7.5), the best total (MEM/SAC under), and NYK on the moneyline instead of the spread. It was about ×4.6 at DraftKings prices, roughly $23 on $5. Model about 29%, book-implied about 22%.

All three legs overlap the 5-fold, so this was more exposure to the same reads, not a hedge. The stake and the exact book prices were never confirmed.

legs.BKN spread: Same read as the 5-fold: model IND by 2.0 against 7.5, with BKN on a back-to-back. Flagged because Haliburton's return made IND's rating stale.
legs.MEM @ SAC: Under total: Model total 230 against 236.5, with Edey out for MEM and three SAC rotation players out.
legs.NYK ML: Model NYK by 10.1, about 79% against 76% implied at -310. A thin edge, but it passed the rule that a favorite's moneyline needs the model at or above the price.

review.summary:
Lost: 1 of 3 (the MEM/SAC under won; BKN and NYK lost).

A short ticket only helps if its legs are independent and clean. This one reused the flagged BKN leg from the 5-fold, so both tickets died on the same read.

Change for next time: a "safer" ticket should leave out the legs the slate flagged, not reuse them.

legs.BKN spread: IND won by 27. See the 5-fold review: the stale IND rating, and the line moving 2 points against us.
legs.NYK ML: ORL won 111-102 on 18 of 42 threes against NYK's 9 of 38. The price still improved before tip (-310 to -270), so the side was market-supported; it lost on variance.

reasoning.summary:
Built from the night-before "Best 6". The team rating model blends 80% last season (regressed ×0.67) with 20% this season (shrunk ×0.25), uses 2.5 points of home court and a 12.5-point margin SD, and is hand-adjusted for injuries and rest. Each leg went in by the gap between the model and the price, after haircuts:
- BKN was haircut because Haliburton's return makes IND's rating stale.
- LAC was haircut because its outs might be under-adjusted.
- Totals were taken at about half their raw edge, because the totals model is unproven.

LAL @ UTA and DET @ PHI were left out. The MEM/SAC under replaced SAC +3.5 because SAC's early form disagreed with the side.

Bet365's bet builder paired BKN +7.5 with the IND/BKN under at +275, more than straight multiplication (about +250). The 5-fold paid +4695: $5 to $239.78. Book-implied about 2%, model about 3.7%.

legs.BKN spread: Model IND by only 2.0 against a 7.5 line, the biggest gap on the slate. BKN was on the second night of a back-to-back and missing Mikel Brown Jr. Downgraded to a slight lean: Haliburton was back from the Achilles with no published minutes limit, and IND's 2025-26 rating came from a season without him.
legs.IND @ BKN: Under total: The model total was 227 against 231.5, with BKN tired on a back-to-back. It was a deliberate pairing with BKN +7.5: a slow, low-scoring game helps both.
legs.LAC spread: Model OKC by 11 against 14.5. LAC was missing Beal, Ingram and Strus. OKC had two days' rest.
legs.NYK spread: Model NYK by 10.1 against 7.5. ORL was without Banchero, Isaac and Penda. This was the only favorite side the model rated above the market.
legs.TOR @ MIN: Under total: Model total 227. Bet365 offered 232.5, a point better than DraftKings' 231.5, which raised the model's chance to about 56.5%.
legs.MEM @ SAC: Under total: Model total 230 against 236.5. MEM was without Edey, and SAC was missing Simmons, Cardwell and Raynaud.

review.summary:
Lost: 3 of 5 folds hit. The IND/BKN bet builder and NYK -7.5 lost; LAC +14.5, the TOR/MIN under and the MEM/SAC under won.

The process was mostly right by the closing line: 5 of 7 graded legs beat the close. The totals beat it by 2-4 points, and the TOR/MIN under won by 21. The ticket died on the one leg the slate itself had flagged, and the bet builder made that one bad read cost two legs.

Changes for next time:
- A leg marked "verify" or "stale rating" doesn't go on the ticket until the flag is cleared.
- Don't put a flagged side inside a same-game builder.

legs.BKN spread: IND won 136-109. Haliburton played 31 minutes and scored 24 with no limit, so IND's stale rating was exactly the risk the slate named. The line moved from 7.5 to 5.5 before tip: the market saw it, and this was the only leg on the ticket with negative closing-line value.
legs.IND @ BKN: Under total: 245 points. It was tied to the BKN read: IND made 21 of 43 threes, so the game was never slow.
legs.NYK spread: ORL won 111-102 outright. Banchero did sit, so no fact was missed. NYK shot 9 of 38 from three (24%) against ORL's 18 of 42. That's shooting variance, though the model's NYK by 10 was also too high. The leg still beat the close by a point.

reasoning.summary:
One leg per game, added in order of model edge. The rating model blends last season and this season, adds 2.5 points of home court, and uses a 12.5-point margin SD. It's hand-adjusted for confirmed outs, back-to-backs, and stale ratings after roster moves (Giannis MIL → MIA). It applied the 10-23 rule: no favorite moneyline unless the model's probability is at or above the price.

At the 5:50 PM recheck, DAL moved to +14.5, ATL flipped from a 1.5-point favorite to a 1.5-point underdog with no injury news, and NOP and MIL held. ATL was marked as the flagged leg. The user placed it at Bet365 for $10 at +2368, to return $246.80 (book-implied about 4.1%, model about 10%).

legs.CHI ML: Model CHI by 5.7, 68% against 56.5% implied. The biggest moneyline edge on the slate. WAS was missing Dybantsa, Vukcevic and Watkins; CHI was without Claxton, and both teams were on a back-to-back. numberFire agreed (66%), but FanDuel listed WAS -1.5, so the books disagreed.
legs.ATL ML: Model ATL by 2.9, 59% against 53.5%. HOU was without Adams and VanVleet. By tip, the line had flipped to HOU -1.5 with no injury found, which is market movement against us.
legs.DAL spread: Model SAS by 8.5 with Flagg out, against 13.5 (14.5 at placement). Media disagreed strongly (numberFire SAS 80%, Covers 78%), with no missed fact found. The model shrinks margins, so it leans toward big underdogs by design.
legs.NOP spread: Model DEN by 7 against 11.5. DEN was without Cam Johnson, Strawther and S. Jones. NOP was on a back-to-back at altitude, already priced into the model.
legs.MIL spread: Model PHI by 9.5 against 12.5. MIL's rating was cut for losing Giannis. LeBron was out for PHI, and Embiid's status was uncertain.

review.summary:
Lost: 2 of 5 (NOP +11.5 and MIL +12.5 won).

Both big-underdog spreads covered. All three losers had a warning attached before tip:
- CHI's rating was built on last season, and WAS's early form was better.
- ATL's line flipped against us.
- DAL had strong media disagreement and the model's built-in lean toward underdogs.

Change for next time: legs flagged at the final review come off the ticket. The ticket shrinks rather than keeping a flagged leg.

legs.CHI ML: WAS won 124-120. This is the stale-rating failure: last season's numbers rated CHI well above WAS, but WAS's 2026-27 form was better. The 20% current-season weight was too small this early. The next day's slate tested moving it to 35%.
legs.ATL ML: HOU won 121-114. The line flip from ATL -1.5 to HOU -1.5 with no news was the market telling us something. On 10-24 the market was right.
legs.DAL spread: SAS won by 16, against 14.5. The media read (SAS 78-80%) was closer than the model. The model's shrink toward zero makes very large spreads look like underdog value more often than they are.

reasoning.summary:
The `matchup-prop-research` sweep over every prop in all 12 games. Each leg was checked through four lenses:
- **A, player baseline:** 2025-26 games with his current team only.
- **B, defense vs position:** what the opponent allows to his position.
- **C, vs this opponent:** his record against this team.
- **D, game environment:** total, pace and confirmed outs.

A leg was dropped if its role had shrunk, any lens contradicted it, the price was shorter than -250, or fewer than 2 books offered it. Probabilities were shrunk halfway toward the market.

Bet365 wasn't offering unders that night, so this is the overs-only version: one leg per game except HOU @ SAS, plus Sengun as an optional seventh. It paid +3,282 at reference prices, $169 on $5. Book-implied 3.0%, model about 5.4%.

legs.Josh Hart over reb+ast (alt): Hit this line in 73% of 86 games last season (87% in the last 15), averaging 12.5. The 223 total was the lowest on the slate, which suits a rebounding leg.
legs.Duncan Robinson over 3PM: Hit 63% last season (73% in the last 15), averaging 2.9 threes. MIA gives shooting guards the most threes in the league (1.17× average). Plus money (+102).
legs.Luka Doncic over assists (alt): Hit 75% at this line, and 67% against LAC (n6), averaging 8.3. Flagged: LAL was favored by 9, so a blowout could cut his minutes.
legs.Alperen Sengun over assists (alt): Hit 73% (73% in the last 15), averaging 6.1. A Strong-tier leg, and the second leg in HOU @ SAS.
legs.Pascal Siakam over PRA: Averaged 34.4 PRA, hitting 58% (60% in the last 15), with 39 in the opener. Upgraded because DAL's frontcourt was thin (Lively and Aldama out) and IND was missing McConnell, so his usage should rise.
legs.Jabari Smith Jr. over PRA (alt): Hit 82% at this alt line (100% in the last 15), averaging 24.7, with 36 in the opener. Strong tier.
legs.Desmond Bane over pts+reb (alt): Hit 75%, averaging 24.2, with 23 in the opener. ORL was without Anthony Black and Isaac, which means more on-ball work for Bane.

review.summary:
Lost: 4 of 7 (Hart, Robinson, Doncic and Sengun won).

Minutes were fine for the winners. The three losers each had a script problem the sweep under-weighted:
- Siakam and Bane were on the losing side of blowouts and lost minutes.
- Siakam's over was also tied to IND ML on the other ticket that night, so one IND loss hurt both tickets.

PRA overs went 0-4 across 10-22 and 10-23. Props overall were 9-16 at about 60% implied, the clearest leak of the week.

Changes for next time:
- For a player over, check the losing-side blowout risk, not just the winning side.
- Don't hold a team's moneyline and its players' overs on separate tickets unless that correlation is deliberate.
- Keep props off parlays until the prop record beats its prices.

legs.Pascal Siakam over PRA: 29 PRA (23/3/3) in 29 minutes. DAL won by 16, so IND's starters sat late. It lost on minutes from the game script, not on role.
legs.Jabari Smith Jr. over PRA (alt): 13 PRA (7/5/1) in 34 minutes. Full minutes but a bad shooting night. The alt line's 82% hit rate came from last season's role.
legs.Desmond Bane over pts+reb (alt): 7 P+R (5/2) in 27 minutes, 1 of 9 from three. ORL lost by 22, so another blowout cut his minutes.

reasoning.summary:
Version 2 of the 12-game sides sweep, re-run after the Giannis trade (MIL → MIA) made two ratings stale. MIL +1.5 and DET dropped to coin flips and were left off this 9-leg. HOU +5.5 was left off as the weakest leg. The rest were moneylines on favorites the model liked, plus two underdog spreads where the model disagreed with the market. Media was checked last and could move confidence by at most one step.

It was $5 at DraftKings, about ×65.4 (about $327). Book-implied about 1.5%.

legs.ATL ML (v2): CHA was without Knueppel, C. White and G. Williams. The model went from CHA +2.8 before injuries to about even. Sportsmole and Dimers agreed.
legs.TOR ML (v2): Model TOR by 6.7, matching the market's 6.5. WAS was without Dybantsa.
legs.MIN ML (v2): ORL was without Black and Isaac. Media agreed.
legs.BOS ML (v2): Model BOS by 2.7 against 2.5, with D. Carter out for BOS. Media mostly agreed.
legs.IND ML (v2): DAL was without Lively, Aldama and C. Martin, and media (Sportsmole) agreed. Our own model had IND by only 2.6 against a 6.5 market.
legs.NOP spread (v2): Model NOP by 0.5 against +2.5. UTA was without Nurkic, and NOP had won all 5 meetings over two seasons.
legs.LAL ML (v2): LAC was missing Beal, Ingram and Strus.
legs.MEM spread (v2): GSW was without Butler, Porzingis and Moody. The model leaned MEM; Dimers and the public leaned GSW.
legs.POR ML (v2): SAC was missing Simmons, Raynaud and Cardwell. POR was 3-0 against SAC last season.

review.summary:
Lost: 8 of 9. IND ML was the only miss.

Game sides went 10-2 that night overall. Where the data disagreed with media (HOU, NOP, MEM), the data won all three. The one loser was a favorite the model rated well below its price. It went on the ticket because it was the favorite and media agreed, not because there was an edge.

This created the standing rule: a favorite's moneyline goes on a ticket only when the model's probability is at or above the implied price. POR and LAL were the same mistake. They won, but at -325 and -380 the model rated both well below the price.

legs.IND ML (v2): DAL won 121-105 at IND. The model's 2.6 against the market's 6.5 was about 58% against 69% implied, so this was a negative-value leg we knew about. Every ticket built that night that included IND lost on this leg alone.
